title: Rogue throwing: 't' missile command (weapons.c missile/do_motion/fall)
description: Port weapons.c missile(): throw a weapon in a direction (reuses get_dir). do_motion flies it straight until it reaches a monster, wall, or door; on a monster it resolves as a thrown fight (roll_em hurl=TRUE: hurl damage, launcher bonus when the matching bow is wielded, else wield damage for an un-launched missile), thunk/bounce messages, kill handling. On miss or no monster it falls (fallpos) to a nearby FLOOR/PASSAGE cell or vanishes. Part of krogue-m07.
close_reason: Ported weapons.c missile/do_motion/fall as ThrowEffects + the 't' command in RogueGame. do_motion flies the weapon straight until a monster/wall/door; a monster is fought as a thrown blow (roll_em hurl=TRUE: hurl dice, launcher bonus only while the matching bow is wielded, else feeble wield dice for an un-launched arrow; thrown enchant counts, rings don't, no +4 sleeping bonus per krogue-aki), thunk/bounce + defeated messages, XP/despawn on kill, weapon spent on a landing hit. Miss/no-monster falls (fallpos reservoir over FLOOR/PASSAGE 3x3, never the hero) or vanishes. Cursed wielded weapon refuses; un-cursed one is unwielded first. 4 tests, 231 green, ktlint clean.

title: Rogue stairs: descend '>' / ascend '<' + level regeneration
description: command.c d_level/u_level: '>' on the down-stair generates and enters the next dungeon level (LevelFactory currently builds only level 1; needs multi-level world + per-level fog already supported by ZoneFog), '<' goes up. Status line dungeon level becomes dynamic. Wandering-monster depth + monster scaling (lev_add) already key off depth. Precursor to the Amulet win/ascend (krogue-5yu). a4d wired the rest of the command set but left stairs to this.
notes:
Implemented (krogue-go8).

ENGINE (korogue): GameWorld zone registry is now mutable — addZone/removeZone over a stable live-view map, so zone-scoped systems (lighting/perception/movement) and the MapPanel that captured world.zones at wiring time see additions/removals with no rebuild. ZoneFog.forget(zoneId) drops a departed level's fog. New tests: GameWorldTest (5), ZoneFog forget (2). ADR-0016.

ROGUE EXAMPLE (korogue-rogue): new headless Dungeon coordinator owns the one world + persistent player; descend()/ascend() generate a fresh zone (LevelFactory.addLevel), relocate the player (only ZoneMember+Position change), despawn the old zone's occupants and removeZone it (Rogue's new_level frees the level). Each visit is a unique zone id => fresh fog. LevelFactory generalized (create + addLevel share populate; ItemLore rolled once). Depth read live: status line 'Level N' (Dungeon.levelLabel) and WanderingMonsterEffect depth supplier scale to the current level; monster treasure gated by atMaxLevel (level>=max_level). Commands: '>' (Shift+.) d_level, '<' (Shift+,) u_level; stairs don't tick the world (after=FALSE) so the shell re-primes lighting/perception. New DungeonTest (7).

DEFERRED to krogue-5yu (faithful u_level): the Amulet gate + ascend-to-win. '<' on the stair currently reports 'your way is magically blocked' (no amulet yet); Dungeon.ascend() regeneration is fully implemented and tested, so 5yu just flips the gate (and adds the level-0 total_winner).
close_reason: Stairs + multi-level regeneration done; engine + rogue tests green, ktlint clean, ADR-0016 recorded. Amulet gate/win deferred to krogue-5yu as planned.

title: Rogue monster special attacks on hit: steal, drain, rust, freeze, breath
description: fight.c attack()'s per-monster on-hit effects: aquator rust_armor, ice-monster freeze (no_command), rattlesnake str-drain, wraith level-drain, vampire maxhp-drain, flytrap hold (vf_hit), leprechaun steal gold, nymph steal item; plus the dragon flame breath (do_chase fire_bolt). Deferred from krogue-c9m and krogue-d5b: each needs a model that doesn't exist yet — equipped armor, no_command/turn-skip, purse, ISHELD, status effects — most landing with item effects (krogue-m07). RogueCombatSystem has the hit hook to dispatch from.

title: Engine: feature/prefab-based world-gen (entity-aware seam + Prefab stamping + generators registry)
description: Today's world-gen extensibility is a single primitive seam: ZoneFeatureGenerator = (Grid<Tile>, Random) -> Vector2Int, applied via Zone.Builder.addFeature, with one built-in (randomWalkCave). Limitations surfaced building the Rogue generator (krogue-c20): (1) terrain-only — the seam can only mutate Grid<Tile>, with no way to place ENTITIES (monsters, gold, items, traps), so real generators bypass it; (2) no prefab/room primitive — nothing to define a parameterized structure (e.g. a 2-5 x 2-5 'shack') and stamp it; (3) no placement framework — no overlap/spacing/density/try-N/bounds-fit; (4) no generator registry — unlike strategies/senses/perception/calculators (first-class GameModule registries, ADR-0014), world-gen has no resolve-by-id, save/load-aware registry. Goal: an entity-aware generator seam (operate on Zone.Builder + an entity sink, or a richer build context), a Prefab/room-stamp primitive with placement constraints, and a GameModule.generators registry. Acceptance test: a 'shack stamper' that scatters variable-size single-room structures across a zone with no overlap. Informed by the bespoke c20 Rogue generator (faithful 3x3-grid port stays example-side; this is the complementary general capability — see ADR-0012 'engine pieces surfaced by the Rogue example' pattern). Likely warrants an ADR.

title: MapPanel renders Perceived; relocate view distance (supersedes f50)
description: Per ADR-0015. MapPanel is handed a chosen observer's Perceived and draws it; it no longer computes LOS-and-lit or owns maximumVisibilityDistance (that moves onto the Sight component, superseding the interim krogue-f50). The rendered observer becomes a presentation choice (player by default; companion/faction views fall out). Wire the Rogue example onto the perception model (player gets a Sight).
close_reason: MapPanel renders a chosen observer's Perceived (default: player); dropped LOS-and-lit and maximumVisibilityDistance (now Sight.radius), finishing krogue-f50->ADR-0015. PerceptionSystem wired after LightingSystem in both demo and Rogue example; player gets Sight()+Perceived(). LineOfSightCalculator made a fun interface. Engine 356 tests + rogue example build green. Force-closed past the soft dep on krogue-1my.3 (concealment): the two are independent — invisible-monster hiding already works via Perceived.entities once 1my.3 lands its Invisible/Blind components; no rendering change needed there.

title: Concealment + tags + piercing + suppressors (two-phase)
description: Per ADR-0015. Concealment components on targets (Invisible) carrying tags they conceal from; senses may declare pierces-tags (see-invisible). Observer suppressor components (Blind) negate tags; suppressors are components (not removal) so a transient blind effect is scheduler-expirable (krogue-6uq). Implement the suppress phase: remove sense contributions whose tags are negated, unless a contributing sense pierces. Tags are string ids with engine constants; no tag registry.
notes: Two-phase reveal/suppress ALGORITHM already landed in 1my.1 (StandardPerception), along with the Suppressor/Concealment MARKER interfaces and Contribution carrying tags/pierces; the algorithm fully handles suppressors, concealments, and piercing generically. This task ADDS: concrete components (Invisible: Concealment{visual}; Blind/Dazzled: Suppressor{visual}; future Silenced{vibration}), engine tag-id constants, piercing senses/modifiers (see-invisible, true-sight) [coordinate with 1my.2 senses], scheduler-expirable transient suppressors (krogue-6uq wiring), GameModule registration, and scenario tests (invisible monster, blindness restore-on-expire).
close_reason: Concrete suppress-phase payload: Invisible (Concealment{visual}), Blind/Dazzled (Suppressor{visual}) as dataless data-objects + TrueSight built-in sense piercing {visual} (sees invisible, unblinded by design — uniform piercing). Registered for save/load + senses in engineDefaults. Transient blindness scheduler-expirable via fuse removing Blind (krogue-6uq). 10 new tests (TrueSightSense unit + PerceptionScenarioTest E2E); full suite + ktlint green. Completes epic krogue-1my.

title: Senses: opt-in components + Sense contributor registry + engine senses
description: Per ADR-0015 + ADR-0014. Senses are opt-in data components (Sight, Darkvision, Tremorsense, Telepathy) interpreted by Sense contributors registered by id in GameModule (module.sense(id, impl)); no sense contributes unless the observer has its component. Each sense declares tags ({visual, light-dependent}, etc.). Engine ships the common senses; games register their own. Move the view-distance (sight radius) onto the Sight component (it is per-observer and mutable).
notes: Senses registry SEAM already exists (added in 1my.1): GameModule.senses (Registry<Sense>) + .sense(id, impl) builder, currently empty. This task ADDS the concrete engine sense COMPONENTS (Sight, Darkvision, Tremorsense, Telepathy as SenseComponent types), their Sense CONTRIBUTORS (with tags + LOS/lightMap reads — note: no LOS registry yet; MapPanel holds losCalculator directly, decide where the sight sense gets its LOS calc), engine tag-id constants, and registers them in GameModule.engineDefaults(). Each sense = its own component type (ECS keys by concrete type).
close_reason: Added engine sense components (Sight/Darkvision/Tremorsense/Telepathy) as opt-in SenseComponent types, their Sense contributors (tags + LOS/lighting/radius reveal), PerceptionTags constants, registered in engineDefaults() with LOS injected via SymmetricShadowCaster. View distance moved onto Sight.radius. Components registered for save/load. 16 new tests, 353 total green.

title: Perception core: PerceptionModel, Perceived, StandardPerception
description: Per ADR-0015. Add the perception layer skeleton: a Perceived result (perceived cells + entities), a PerceptionModel interface (perceive(observer, world) -> Perceived) resolved via GameModule (new registry), and a default StandardPerception implementing the two-phase reveal/suppress model. A PerceptionSystem writes a derived Perceived component per-tick for observers that need it each frame (per-observer caching, like lightMap). Query is the primitive; cache is the optimization.
close_reason: Perception core landed: perception package (Perceived, Contribution, Sense/SenseComponent, Suppressor/Concealment, PerceptionModel, StandardPerception two-phase model), PerceptionSystem per-observer cache, GameModule senses+perceptionModels registries. 16 tests added (337 total, green). Ships inert pending 1my.2 (senses) / 1my.3 (concealments).

title: Perception & visibility model (ADR-0015)
description: Implement the three-layer visibility model from ADR-0015: illumination (exists) + line-of-sight (exists) + a new observer-relative perception layer. Perception = composable senses (opt-in data components interpreted by registered Sense contributors), concealment components carrying tags, sense-pierces-tags, a two-phase reveal-then-suppress execution, suppressor components (blindness, scheduler-expirable), per-observer query with per-observer caching, and MapPanel rendering a chosen observer's Perceived result. Engine ships StandardPerception + common senses so simple games just add a Sight component. Governed by ADR-0014 (pluggable policy, fixed mechanism).
close_reason: All 4 children complete: perception core + two-phase reveal/suppress (1my.1), built-in senses (1my.2), MapPanel renders Perceived (1my.4), concealment/piercing/suppressors (1my.3). Three-layer visibility model per ADR-0015 shipped: illumination + LOS + observer-relative perception via composable senses, tag-based concealment/suppression with piercing, per-observer cache. Engine ships StandardPerception + Sight/Darkvision/TrueSight/Tremorsense/Telepathy + Invisible/Blind/Dazzled.

title: MapPanel: optional (uncapped) view distance
description: MapPanel.maximumVisibilityDistance is a non-nullable Double (default 30), so every game gets a hard circular visibility cap even though the LineOfSightCalculator interface already accepts a nullable maxViewDistance (null = no cap, honored by SymmetricShadowCaster). A game with global/room lighting wants visibility limited only by walls, not distance. Make the field Double? (default 30.0, null = unlimited) and pass it through. Surfaced by the Rogue example: a lit room was clipped to a 30-tile disc, which read as non-global. Discovered via krogue-hhe.
close_reason: MapPanel.maximumVisibilityDistance is now Double?, default null (uncapped/walls-only). Test added. Note: view distance ultimately moves onto a per-observer Vision component in the visibility rework.

title: Label widget: single line of text in the UI toolkit
description: The UI toolkit (ADR-0011) has Frame/BarWidget/LogPanel/Menu/MapPanel/Dialog but no plain text label, so a status line must be hand-rolled (the Rogue example wrote a custom StatusLine widget). Add a Label widget: draws a () -> String on the top row of its bounds, truncated to fit, fg/bg/z configurable. Widely useful for status lines, captions, HUD readouts. Refactor the Rogue example to use it. Discovered building the Rogue example (krogue-hhe).
close_reason: Label widget (single live text line) in the UI toolkit; Rogue example uses it. Tests added.

title: Direction enum: 8 compass directions as a grid primitive
description: Movement, AI, FOV, and throwing all hand-roll dx/dy steps (WanderStrategy's STEPS list, HuntPlayerStrategy's coerceIn, the Rogue example's MOVES map). Add a Direction enum to com.sletmoe.korogue.utilities: 8 compass dirs with (dx,dy) unit steps, opposite, from(Vector2Int), and companion CARDINAL/DIAGONAL plus ofStep/between for turning a delta into a single grid step. Add a MoveIntent(Direction) constructor. Dogfood it in WanderStrategy. Discovered building the Rogue example (krogue-hhe) per the 'find missing engine pieces' directive.
close_reason: Direction enum (8 compass dirs, opposite/from/CARDINAL/DIAGONAL/ofStep/between) + MoveIntent(Direction); WanderStrategy dogfoods it. Tests added.

title: Ambient light / global illumination mode (lightMap baseline)
description: Lighting is purely emitter-driven: LightingSystem fills each zone's lightMap to null and only LightEmitter entities light cells, and MapPanel hides any cell whose lightMap is null. So a roguelike that doesn't model light (Rogue, and many others) has no clean way to render — it must fake a giant LightEmitter on the player. Add an ambient-light baseline to LightingSystem (ambientLight: LightValue? = null): fill the lightMap with the ambient value instead of null, so emitters blend on top and, with a full-white ambient, the whole zone is uniformly lit ('global illumination' / fullbright). Add LightValue.FULLBRIGHT preset. Backward compatible (default null = current point-light behavior). Discovered while scaffolding the Rogue example (krogue-hhe).
close_reason: LightingSystem gains ambientLight baseline + LightValue.FULLBRIGHT; global illumination without faking emitters. Tests added.

title: Fixed-timestep RealTimeLoop (decouple continuous ticks from render FPS)
description: RealTimeLoop (krogue-lhw) currently ticks the world once per render frame, so the continuous game speed is tied to frame rate (faster machine / higher FPS = faster monsters; frame hitches stutter the sim). Decouple it: accumulate per-frame wall-clock delta and advance the world at a fixed timestep (e.g. every N ms) independent of render FPS, with a max-catch-up cap to avoid the spiral of death after a long frame. Requires threading a deltaMs into GameLoop.advance (currently advance(tick) has no time arg) — e.g. advance(deltaMs, tick); TurnBasedLoop ignores it. Then real-time AI can act every fixed tick and the per-tick act-chance throttle could be dropped. Engine change in com.sletmoe.korogue.loop.
close_reason: RealTimeLoop is now a fixed-timestep accumulator (stepMs/maxCatchUpSteps); deltaMs threaded through Game.onTick -> GameLoop.advance. World speed is FPS-independent. Tests + build green.

title: Fold kotile into the korogue repo as a Gradle subproject (monorepo)
description: Decision: korogue + kotile become one repo (separate maven publishes). Plan (verify build at each step): 1) git subtree add --prefix=kotile ~/development/kotile mainline (preserve history); 2) remove kotile's nested settings.gradle.kts + duplicate wrapper (gradlew, gradle/, bin/) so only the root build governs; 3) root settings.gradle.kts: drop includeBuild("../kotile")+dependencySubstitution, add include(":kotile:library", ":kotile:demo"); 4) engine dep com.sletmoe:kotile -> project(":kotile:library"); 5) reconcile plugin management (kotlin 2.3.21/dokka 2.2.0/foojay already align; root settings already has them) and keep kotile group=com.sletmoe (artifact kotile) vs engine group=com.sletmoe.korogue; decide whether engine stays at root or moves to :engine; 6) rework CI workflows (remove sibling kotile checkout); 7) verify ./gradlew check for both + the demo runs. Not blocking: composite build works today. See ADR-0011/0012 context.
close_reason: Folded kotile into the korogue repo via git subtree (history preserved, commit 2c451cc): :kotile:library + :kotile:demo subprojects, separate maven coords (com.sletmoe:kotile). Replaced includeBuild composite with include(); engine deps project(:kotile:library); gradle.properties carries gdxVersion/kotestVersion; removed kotile nested settings/wrapper; CI sibling-checkout dropped; docs updated. Verified ./gradlew check (engine+kotile) + ./gradlew run.

title: Rogue commands + UI: full command set, status line, messages
description: Port command.c: movement/run/rest, pickup, inventory, quaff/read/wield/wear/put-on/zap/throw/eat/drop, search, up/down stairs, help, options. Status line (level/HP/str/gold/AC/hunger/exp) and the message line, on the krogue UI toolkit + turn-on-input loop (krogue-lhw).
notes: Slice 2 (inventory + equipment state) done: player starts with Rogue's init_player kit (StartingPack: food, worn ring mail AC6, wielded +1,+1 mace, +1 bow, arrows) + Purse; ItemLore singleton rolled per game (LevelFactory); Equipment.profileOf wires wielded weapon (dice+pluses) and worn armor (AC) into RogueCombatSystem — closes the c9m weapon/armor hook; RoguePickupSystem (gold->purse, items->pack via add_pack, lore-named messages) registered after combat, replacing the unused engine PickupSystem; status line shows real gold + armour as 10-AC from worn gear; 'i' inventory overlay (modal) listing the pack with equip tags via inv_name. +9 tests (StartingPack 4, Equipment 2, RoguePickup 3); 143 total, green. Remaining: equipment-CHANGE commands (w/W/T/P/R/d + item-selection UI), item-use commands (q/r/e/z/t/identify -> krogue-m07), stairs >/< (descend), floor item placement (put_things), run/search.
close_reason: Rogue command set + UI delivered across three slices on krogue-rogue. Slice 1: three-band screen (message line via RogueLog/RogueMessages formatting fight.c hit/miss/killed + pickups + level-ups, erase-on-input; full rogue.c status line) + '.' rest + '?' help overlay. Slice 2: init_player starting pack + Purse, ItemLore singleton, Equipment.profileOf wiring wielded weapon + worn armor into RogueCombatSystem (closed c9m's weapon/armor hook), RoguePickupSystem (gold->purse, items->pack), 'i' inventory overlay with equip tags. Slice 3: equipment-change commands w/W/T (wield/wear/take-off) with a letter-keyed item-selection modal (Chooser), Shift-disambiguated. 143 tests green, ktlint clean throughout. Remaining command set is blocked on other systems and tracked separately: item-use q/r/e/z/t/identify -> krogue-m07; drop 'd' + floor-item placement + pickup-on-move -> krogue-rx2; stairs >/< + descend -> krogue-go8; rings P/R need obtainable rings (m07/rx2); run(HJKL)/search/options are minor polish.

title: Rogue combat: to-hit, damage rolls, AC, strength/level bonuses, special attacks
description: Port fight.c: swing/roll_em to-hit vs AC, damage strings (roll N d S +plus), strength and experience bonuses, weapon/armor pluses, thrown weapons, monster special attacks on hit. Extends krogue CombatSystem.
close_reason: Ported fight.c swing/roll_em as a pure Combat object (to-hit vs AC, damage-string parsing incl. multi-attack and 0x0/%%%x0 placeholders, strength to-hit/damage bonuses, weapon/ring hplus/dplus params, sleeping +4) plus RogueCombatSystem wiring AttackIntent -> damage/Health, regen-quiet reset both sides, and experience-on-kill + despawn (killed). Registered after MovementSystem in RogueGame. 18 tests (CombatTest 13, RogueCombatSystemTest 5), all green. Deferred to existing beads: per-monster special attacks on hit (rust/freeze/drain/steal/hold) need status/equip/purse models -> krogue-d5b/m07; sleeping +4 needs monster waking state -> krogue-d5b; reading weapon/armor pluses from equipped Pack + thrown weapons -> krogue-m07/a4d (Combat math already honors the pluses).

title: Rogue monster AI: chase/flee/greed, behavior flags, special abilities
description: Port chase.c + behavior flags: chase the player (runto/find_dest), flee when scared, ISMEAN wake-on-enter, ISGREED protect gold, ISFLY/ISREGEN/ISHASTE/ISSLOW, confused/held/invisible; special abilities (steal gold/items, drain str/level/maxhp, breath, rust, freeze, etc.). As BehaviorStrategies on krogue.
close_reason: Ported chase.c's chase/diag_ok/dist as a pure Chase object (greedy 8-neighbour descent to min squared distance, faithful rnd(++plcnt) tie-break, diag-corner legality, target cell is a valid destination so closing a gap becomes a MovementSystem bump -> RogueCombatSystem attack) and ChaseStrategy (BehaviorStrategy): MEAN-vs-timid aggro gate, bat/phantom innate-confusion random moves, monster-occupancy avoidance, same-zone gate. Wired: MonsterFactory tags Behavior(rogue-chase), RogueModule registers the strategy bound to world.zones, RogueGame runs BehaviorSystem before MovementSystem. 13 tests (ChaseTest 7, ChaseStrategyTest 6) green; ktlint clean. Monsters now hunt and melee the player end-to-end. Deferred (engine seam / missing models), filed + linked: latched wake/scared/confused -> krogue-aki; HASTE/FLY/SLOW double/half-move -> krogue-upf; greed gold-guard + room/door routing -> krogue-0yr; on-hit special attacks -> krogue-2u9.

title: Rogue monsters: 26-monster table, depth spawning, wandering monsters
description: Port monsters.c: the A-Z monster table (name, carry prob, flags, stats, damage). Depth-based selection (randmonster, lev_mons/wand_mons, e_levels), per-level population, and wandering-monster spawns via the scheduler. Monsters carry pack items.
close_reason: Monster data + spawning layer (krogue-rogue): MonsterTable (26-monster A-Z table verbatim from extern.c monsters[]; lvl_mons/wand_mons + randmonster from monsters.c, depth-clamped selection), Monster component + MonsterFlag enum (MEAN/FLY/REGEN/INVIS/GREED/HASTE), MonsterFactory (new_monster stat rolls: roll(lvl,8) HP, lev_add depth scaling, exp_add award, give_pack carried items, rnd_thing xeroc disguise; ISINVIS wired to engine Invisible concealment). Per-room population in LevelGenerator.do_rooms (80% gold-guarded / 25% plain, randmonster, MonsterSpot) spawned by LevelFactory. Wandering spawns via scheduler: WanderingMonsterEffect (rollwand/swander cadence — every 4th turn, 1/6, then spread(70) lull) with savable Wandering singleton; registered in RogueModule, started by RogueGame. 16 new tests (90 total), ktlint clean, build green. AI (d5b) and combat (c9m) consume these but are out of scope. Not committed (conservative profile).

notes:
WANDS (do_zap offensive bolts + get_dir) done. THROWING done (krogue-3be): weapons.c missile/do_motion/fall as ThrowEffects + the 't' command, reusing get_dir and Combat.rollEm (hurl damage, launcher bonus, thunk/bounce + defeated messages, fallpos drop or vanish; un-launched arrows do feeble wield damage). REMAINING in m07: (1) detection + magic-mapping scrolls/potions (S_MAP, S_FDET, monster/magic detection potions) — need a detection/reveal model over the fog (ZoneFog) and a creature-overlay; (2) the monster-state scrolls — S_CONFUSE (CANHUH), S_HOLD (ISHELD), S_AGGR (aggravate), and S_SCARE's flee-when-dropped — all blocked on the AI-state component (krogue-aki); S_SCARE *reading* (just 'maniacal laughter', not identified) and S_CREATE (spawn a monster near the hero) and S_PROTECT (ISPROT flag) are self-contained and portable next; (3) eat food / hunger (krogue-fwh). title: Timed-effects scheduler (daemons & fuses) for the turn loop
description: Rogue drives most timed behaviour through a daemon/fuse scheduler (rogue.h/daemons.c): one-shot 'fuses' that fire after N turns and recurring 'daemons' that run every turn (regen, hunger, status-effect expiry, ring effects, wandering-monster spawns). Add a general turn-keyed scheduler to the krogue engine: schedule one-shot and recurring callbacks/effects by turn count, cancel/lengthen them, advance on each world turn, and make it part of save state (so timers resume). Pairs with krogue-lhw (turn-on-input loop). The Rogue example (krogue-sdh) is its first consumer.
close_reason: Added turn-keyed Scheduler (fuses/daemons, cancel/lengthen) + TimedEffect extension point + SchedulerSystem; GameModule effects registry; serializable SchedulerState round-tripped via SaveCodec (timers resume across save/load). Demo wired (no effects yet). 17 new tests, ktlint clean.

title: Turn-on-input loop (replace per-frame ticking)
description: The ECS world currently ticks once per render frame (MyGame.onTick), so creatures act ~60x/sec and combat is near-instant (the player can die immediately). AI strategies carry a 2%-per-tick act gate as a band-aid. Replace with a turn-based loop: advance the world only when the player takes an action (move/wait/etc.), so one player action = one world turn and AI acts once per turn (drop the act-gate throttle). This is also a prerequisite for the Rogue example (krogue-sdh), which is turn-based by nature. Touches MyGame's loop (onTick vs input) and BehaviorStrategies' throttle.
close_reason: Closed

title: Dialog + Menu: modal dialogs with selectable buttons
description: Dialog widget: opaque modal panel on a high z-layer; the uncovered area renders dimmed (colors x factor, top-wins compositing per ADR-0011); input routes to the dialog via UiRoot's focus stack. Menu widget: selectable list (highlighted index, up/down + Enter, inverted selection). Add a system/pause menu to the demo (Save / Load / Settings / Exit).
close_reason: Dialog + Menu landed and wired into the demo. Menu: selectable list (up/down wrap, Enter activates, inverted highlight). Dialog: opaque modal box (fill + Frame + content) added to UiRoot modal=true so the root dims layers below and routes input to it. Demo: Esc system menu (resume/save/load/quit, pauses world via ui.hasModal) and a non-cancellable game-over dialog at 0 HP. 8 headless tests (274 total). Verified in-game.

title: MapPanel: confine the zone renderer to a screen rect

title: UI toolkit core: TileSurface seam, Widget/UiRoot, input stack, rect-split
description: Foundation for the krogue UI toolkit (ADR-0011). Define a TileSurface cell-sink interface (put(x,y,z,glyph,fg,bg) + width/height) with an AsciiTileWindow-backed adapter and a fake for tests (makes UI headlessly testable). Add a Widget/Panel base (screen IntRect + z-layer, draws into the surface within its rect), a UiRoot that holds a stack of layers, renders bottom-up in one window.render pass, and routes input to the topmost modal (focus stack) else falls through to gameplay. Rect-split helpers (splitRight/splitBottom). No kotile changes.

title: Wire save/load into the demo (keybinds + file) so it's reachable
description: SaveCodec (entities + terrain + RNG + fog) is implemented and tested but the demo never calls it, so there's no way to actually save/load while playing. Add save/load triggers to MyGame: a save keybind that writes codec.save(world, rng, zoneFog.snapshot()) to a file, and a load keybind that reads it back via codec.load and swaps in the loaded world/RNG/fog, re-registering systems and rebuilding the renderer. Lets us manually verify the whole save/load path, including fog persistence (krogue-k77).
close_reason: Wired save/load into MyGame: F5 saves (codec.save with zoneFog.snapshot()), F9 loads (swaps in loaded world/RNG/fog, re-registers systems, re-resolves player, rebuilds renderer). Verified in-game over 3 save/load cycles incl. across zone transitions; fog persists. Save file gitignored. Save-size (~13MB terrain) filed as krogue-yox.

title: 4f step 3: CBOR save/load codec
description: Per ADR-0009: CBOR (kotlinx-serialization-cbor). @Serializable components; save = envelope{formatVersion, payload} where payload = entities+components + serialized tile grids + currentZoneId + turn counter + RNG state (master seed + stream states). Exclude lightMap + intents. Preserve EntityId + World.nextId. Version-first/payload-second seam (migration deferred, fail-fast on mismatch). save(sink)/load(source) API; game owns triggers/location.
close_reason: CBOR save/load codec (ADR-0009). Added kotlinx-serialization plugin + cbor dep. @Serializable + stable @SerialName discriminators on savable components (Position/ZoneMember/Named/Health/Renderable/Player/LightEmitter/Behavior/Portal) + NormalizedRgb/RenderLayer; Tile @Serializable via GdxColorSerializer (RGBA8888). ComponentRegistry (polymorphic SerializersModule) added to GameModule (component<T>()). RandomState/GameRandomState @Serializable. World.restore/nextEntityId (internal). SaveCodec.save/load over entities+terrain(grids)+RNG+turn+currentZoneId; SaveEnvelope{formatVersion,payload} version-first seam; fail-fast on mismatch; transient components excluded; EntityId+nextId preserved. +2 round-trip tests (218 total). Game owns triggers (not wired into demo).

title: 4f step 2: registry + GameModule (replace stub registries)
description: Hybrid registry per ADR-0009: internal ComponentRegistry (-> kotlinx SerializersModule, stable string discriminators), StrategyRegistry, CalculatorRegistry; a GameModule builder facade (engineDefaults() + consumer additions, coherence validation). Retire LightCalculators/BehaviorStrategies objects; BehaviorSystem/LightingSystem resolve via injected registries. Independently useful before save/load.
close_reason: Added com.sletmoe.krogue.registry: Registry<T> + GameModule (builder facade; engineDefaults() + consumer additions) bundling per-concern strategy/calculator registries (ADR-0009 hybrid iii). Built-in ids moved onto classes (WanderStrategy.ID, HuntPlayerStrategy.ID, Diminishing/GlobalLightValueCalculator.ID). Deleted LightCalculators + BehaviorStrategies stub objects; BehaviorSystem/LightingSystem resolve via injected narrow seams; MyGame builds GameModule.engineDefaults(). ComponentRegistry/SerializersModule deferred to s3 (CBOR). +3 tests.

title: 4f step 1: serializable RNG + named seed streams
description: xoshiro256** generator (serializable 4-long state) + SplitMix64 to derive named sub-streams off a master Long seed. Provide a krogue RNG service: master seed -> stream(name): isolated, deterministic stream; capture/restore each stream's state. Replaces kotlin.random.Random usage in worldgen/placement/AI/combat. Enables shareable seeds + exact-resume RNG (ADR-0009). Independently useful before save/load.
close_reason: Added com.sletmoe.krogue.random: SerializableRandom (xoshiro256** as a kotlin.random.Random with serializable 4-long state), SplitMix64 (seeding + stream-seed derivation), GameRandom (master seed -> named isolated streams; snapshot/restore). Per ADR-0009: shareable deterministic seeds + exact-resume RNG. MyGame draws worldgen/placement from a 'worldgen' stream and AI/combat from a 'gameplay' stream (same master seed => same world). +9 tests (213). Independently useful before save/load.

title: Fix broken GitHub Actions CI (build + Dokka failing on every push)
description: All workflow runs red on mainline: .github/workflows/build.yml and dokka.yml fail on push; pr.yml/release.yml unverified. Diagnose from failing run logs and fix. Track progress in comments so it can be resumed.
close_reason: FIXED — build + Dokka green on mainline (commit da6213c). Root causes: (1) action rot — Java 11 (Gradle 9 needs 17+), archived wrapper-validation-action@v1, Node-20 action versions, 'coretto' typo, dokka V1 task name under V2 mode, stale bucket4k cname; (2) krogue's includeBuild('../kotile') had no kotile on CI; (3) accumulated ktlint violations the broken CI never caught. Fixes: modernized all 4 workflows (setup-java 21, @v4 actions, gradle/actions/wrapper-validation@v4, dokka :dokkaGenerateHtml + build/dokka/html + permissions:contents:write + peaceiris@v4); added git-clone of kotile sibling; made kotile repo PUBLIC (user-approved) so the clone works; ran ktlintFormat. build+Dokka verified GREEN. pr.yml (PR-only) and release.yml (manual dispatch) fixed by the same patterns, verified by inspection not a live run. Note: GitHub warns @v4 actions still run on Node20 (informational, non-failing; GitHub auto-migrates to Node24).

The rest of sticks.c do_zap remains: WS_LIGHT (light the room — needs the dark-room model, krogue-kj5); WS_DRAIN (split half the hero's HP among monsters in the room — needs room membership); and the 'find first monster in the firing line' utility staves WS_INVIS (set ISINVIS), WS_POLYMORPH (rebuild as a random monster via MonsterFactory), WS_HASTE_M/WS_SLOW_M (toggle ISHASTE/ISSLOW — movement effect waits on monster speed krogue-upf), WS_TELAWAY/WS_TELTO (relocate the monster), WS_CANCEL (set a cancelled flag — needs the flag + special-attack gating). title: Rogue remaining ring passives: see-invis, aggravate, regen, sustain str/armor, search, stealth, slow digestion, teleport
description: The four numeric rings (protection, add-strength, dexterity, increase-damage) are wired into combat/strength by the ring put-on/off slice (krogue-m07). The flag rings still need their passive behavior, each gated on a system: R_SEEINVIS (see invisible) -> perception; R_AGGR (aggravate monster, on put-on) -> monster AI wake; R_REGEN (regeneration) -> RegenEffect cadence; R_SUSTSTR (sustain strength) -> block str-drain at poison/dart/monster sites; R_SUSTARM (maintain armor) -> block rust trap/monster; R_SEARCH -> auto-search each turn; R_STEALTH -> monsters don't wake on approach (AI); R_DIGEST (slow digestion) -> hunger clock (krogue-fwh); R_TELEPORT -> random teleport while worn. Rings can already be worn; only the passive effect is deferred.

title: Rogue: floor item placement (put_things) + drop command + pickup-on-move
description: Three interlocking pieces a4d left open. (1) put_things (things.c): the level generator should scatter floor items (not just gold/monster drops) so there's loot to find. (2) drop command 'd': spawn the dropped RogueItem as a floor entity. (3) pickup-on-move: RoguePickupSystem currently sweeps the player's tile every tick, so a dropped item is re-grabbed the same turn and resting on loot keeps 'picking it up'; make pickup fire only when the player steps onto a tile (Rogue's move_on), which also unblocks 'd'. Builds on the inventory/pickup work in a4d.
close_reason: All three pieces on krogue-rogue. (1) put_things (new_level.c): LevelGenerator scatters up to MAXOBJ=9 items, each a 36% roll of ItemFactory.newThing on a free floor cell, carried as ItemSpot in DungeonLayout and spawned by LevelFactory via the new shared FloorItem.spawn (glyph + engine Item marker + RogueItem). (2) pickup-on-move: RoguePickupSystem now fires only when the player enters a new (zone,cell), so resting on loot doesn't repeatedly grab it and a dropped item isn't snatched back the same turn. (3) drop 'd': prompt-select a pack slot, lay one on the floor at the player's feet (FloorItem.spawn), spend a turn. +3 tests (put_things placement x2, move-trigger x1); 154 total, green; ktlint clean. This makes the whole item/equipment/potion system reachable in play: loot can now be found, picked up, equipped, quaffed (krogue-m07), and dropped. Treasure rooms + Amulet gating in put_things left for later; descend/stairs is krogue-go8.

title: Rogue monster AI: gold-guarding greed + room/door routing (needs runtime room metadata)
description: chase.c routes between rooms via the nearest door to the goal (rer/ree/r_exit) and ISGREED monsters guard a room's gold (find_dest to r_gold until taken). ChaseStrategy (krogue-d5b) does pure greedy descent toward the player only, because rooms aren't exposed at runtime — DungeonLayout/Zone carry tiles but not room rectangles/exits/gold-by-room. Expose room metadata from the generator (krogue-c20), then add door-routing + greed find_dest.

title: Rogue monster AI: latched wake/run, scared-flee, confusion-on-hit (needs AI-state component)
description: ChaseStrategy (krogue-d5b) is stateless: aggro is a proximity gate (MEAN range vs adjacent) standing in for Rogue's room-entry wake_monster, and it has no persistent run/scared/confused state because the engine's BehaviorStrategy.decide must be pure (movement-only, no world mutation). To be faithful we need a mutable per-monster AI-state component (ISRUN/ISFLEE/ISHUH/ISTARGET) plus either a richer decision seam or a small AiSystem that transitions it: latched waking, ISFLEE flee-movement (scare scroll/aggravate from krogue-m07), and ISHUH confusion-on-hit. Engine-side seam change likely (korogue repo).

title: Rogue monster speed: HASTE/FLY double-move and SLOW half-move
description: chase.c move_monst runs do_chase up to twice a turn (ISHASTE, and ISFLY when >=3 away) and skips alternate turns when ISSLOW (t_turn toggle). The engine's one-MoveIntent-per-tick model can't express a double step, so ChaseStrategy (krogue-d5b) currently ignores speed. Needs multi-step-per-turn support (engine seam) or a per-monster action-points model.

title: ktlintCheck red: pre-existing violations in rogue item/monster files
description: The korogue-rogue ktlintCheck gate is red from pre-existing violations unrelated to current work: function-signature in item/ItemLore.kt (4) and item/Pack.kt (1); test files MonsterFactoryTest.kt (import-ordering + unused import) and MonsterTableTest.kt (max-line-length). Surfaced while landing combat (krogue-c9m), whose own files are lint-clean. Mirrors the earlier perception-file cleanup (krogue-kn8). Fix: ktlintFormat the offenders and re-run ktlintCheck.
close_reason: Not reproducible: a fresh 'ktlintCheck --rerun-tasks' passes clean and the named files are byte-identical to HEAD. The earlier violation list came from a stale aggregated ktlint report, not the current tree.

title: Rogue: unify dice helpers (LevelGenerator.rnd vs actor/Dice)
description: LevelGenerator has a private rnd(n) (krogue-c20); the player model added a shared Dice object (rnd/roll, krogue-pyh). Both mirror Rogue misc.c rnd. Fold LevelGenerator onto Dice for one source of truth. Pure cleanup, deferred from krogue-pyh to keep that change focused.

title: Magical darkness vs darkvision: distinguish from ordinary unlit (lighting↔perception)
description:
DESIGN DECISION + impl. Known divergence from the 5e-flavoured default (ADR-0015): in 5e, *magical* darkness (the Darkness spell) blocks darkvision while truesight still pierces it; ordinary darkness does not block darkvision. Our model (ADR-0015) makes magical darkness just 'unlit' (lightMap == null) and DarkvisionSense ignores lighting entirely, so in-engine **darkvision penetrates magical darkness** — only Sight (light-dependent) is stopped. Result: an effect that should hard-counter darkvision currently doesn't.

To close the gap faithfully, the LIGHTING layer needs to distinguish 'magical darkness' from plain unlit (e.g. a magical-darkness region marker / a darkness intensity below a floor), and perception needs Darkvision blocked by it while TrueSight pierces it — i.e. magical darkness behaves like a visual *suppressor/concealment of the cell* that only piercing sight beats. This is a lighting↔perception interaction we don't model yet; relates to ADR-0015's 'magical darkness lives in the illumination layer' note and to krogue-0vg (ambient/global light) and krogue-kj5 (room-based visibility).

Not urgent — many roguelikes don't model magical darkness at all. Filed to THINK ABOUT: decide whether the engine should model it as a first-class concept, and if so where the seam lives (lighting marker vs a cell-level concealment tag) before implementing.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded (in ADR-0015 or a new ADR) on whether/how magical darkness is modelled distinctly from unlit; if adopted: a magical-darkness region blocks Sight AND Darkvision but is pierced by TrueSight, with tests; if rejected: documented as an intentional non-goal.
notes: Surfaced 2026-06-13 reviewing perception (krogue-1my) against D&D 5e as the genre default bar. The truesight/blindness and see-invisible behaviour already match 5e; this is the one remaining behavioural divergence. Telepathy naming was reviewed and kept (Brogue/NetHack call the same detect-monsters-through-walls sense 'telepathy'; only tabletop 5e narrows the term to communication).

title: ktlintCheck red: pre-existing violations in perception files
description: `./gradlew ktlintCheck` fails on HEAD (since commit 58ef942, krogue-1my.1/.2), independent of krogue-1my.4. Violations: no-consecutive-comments in EngineSenses.kt:26, SenseComponents.kt:24, Suppression.kt:17 (file-level KDoc immediately followed by a declaration KDoc), and import-ordering in systems/PerceptionSystem.kt:3 (Perceived should precede PerceptionModel). The file-level-overview-KDoc style needs converting to a block comment (or merging); import order is ktlintFormat-fixable. Build's `test` gate is green; only ktlintCheck is affected.
close_reason: Fixed alongside krogue-1my.4: converted the file-overview KDoc blocks in EngineSenses/SenseComponents/Suppression to block comments (no-consecutive-comments), and ktlintFormat fixed the PerceptionSystem import order. ktlintCheck now green.

title: Room-based visibility model (Rogue lit/dark rooms)
description: Rogue's true visibility is room-based: the room you're in is fully revealed if lit, otherwise only your immediate surroundings; corridors show adjacent cells; you never see through walls into unentered rooms. The engine currently offers SymmetricShadowCaster (LOS) and Omniscient (everything). Neither is Rogue-faithful for a multi-room dungeon (shadowcast over-reveals down corridors/through doors; omniscient sees everything). Build a room-aware visibility model once level generation provides room metadata. Depends on krogue-c20. The Rogue example scaffold approximates with uncapped SymmetricShadowCaster for now.

title: Rogue graphical tileset renderer (ASCII vs tiles via config)
description: A sprite-backed rendering selectable by config, sharing the same game logic as the ASCII renderer: plug a tileset backend in behind the TileSurface seam / Renderable (kotile sprite path). Source a suitably-licensed roguelike tileset. ASCII remains the default.

title: Rogue win/lose: Amulet of Yendor, ascend to win, tombstone + score
description: Amulet of Yendor on level 26 (AMULETLEVEL); descend to get it, ascend to the surface to win (total_winner). Death handling + tombstone/scoring (rip.c). Rogue game persists via krogue save/load.
close_reason: Amulet of Yendor placed from AMULETLEVEL (26) down (LevelGenerator put_things + LevelFactory !amulet gate); '<' ascent gated on the amulet and wins off level 1 (total_winner); death->tombstone and win->worth-listing scoring (rip.c) via Score + EndScreen; killer tracked through LastAttacker (save/load registered). Implemented in the korogue-rogue repo.

title: Rogue hunger clock: food, hungry states, starvation
description: Port the hunger clock (daemons.c): food_left, HUNGERTIME/STOMACHSIZE/STARVETIME, hungry/weak/faint states with status messages, and starvation death. Driven by the scheduler.

title: Inventory side panel
description: Bordered side panel listing inventory items (placeholder model for the demo until a real item/inventory system exists). Uses Frame + the scrollable-list logic from LogPanel.
close_reason: Inventory landed with a minimal real item model: Item(name)+Inventory(items) serializable components (registered), PickupSystem (walk onto a non-blocking item -> despawn + add to inventory + ItemPickedUp event), and InventoryPanel widget. Demo: items scattered per zone, sidebar stacks Log over Inventory, pickups logged, round-trips through save/load (verified in-game). 9 tests (286 total). UI epic 6/6.

title: Compact terrain serialization (save files are ~13MB)
description: The demo's save is ~13MB: zones are 200x200 (40k cells each, x2 = 80k tiles), and SaveCodec serializes each cell's full Tile (name string, two colors, booleans) with no interning/RLE — e.g. 'stone wall' written ~34k times per zone (~168 bytes/tile). Walls count as tiles even though randomWalkCave only carves ~6k floors. Options: (1) intern tile prototypes into a per-zone palette + store per-cell index, and/or RLE the row-major grid; (2) revisit demo zone size. Functionally fine today; this is a size/perf follow-up to the 4f save codec.

title: Example package: implement original Rogue as a fully playable game on krogue
description: Faithful Kotlin port of Rogue 5.4.4 on krogue, redistributed under the original BSD-3-Clause with full attribution to Toy/Arnold/Wichman (ADR-0012). Lives in com.sletmoe.krogue.examples.rogue; validates the engine end-to-end and is the reference 'how to build a game on krogue'. Source of truth: ~/Downloads/rogue5.4.4. Engine prereqs (general, not children): krogue-lhw turn loop + a timed-effects scheduler. Decomposed into child tasks; build a minimal playable vertical slice first (generated dungeon, move, pick up, fight, descend), then fill content.

title: Persist fog-of-war memory across save/load
description: ZoneFog (krogue-ro8) keeps per-zone 'previously seen' memory in-session only; it is not written to save files, so a loaded game starts unexplored. Persist fog per zone in the save model/codec (SaveModel + SaveCodec, ADR-0009) so explored areas survive save/load. Decide whether fog belongs in Zone state or a separate per-zone player-knowledge section of the envelope.
close_reason: Fog persists across save/load: added SaveData.fog (per-zone SavedFog, additive/default-empty so old payloads still load — no version bump per ADR-0009), carried by SaveCodec as Map<String,Grid<Boolean>> (codec stays decoupled from the renderer); ZoneFog.snapshot()/restore() bridge it. 4 new tests (codec round-trip + additive default; ZoneFog snapshot/restore), 238 total. Capability is wired+tested but the demo doesn't yet trigger save/load.

title: Per-zone fog-of-war memory (renderer rebuilt on zone change)
description: 4e rebuilds KotileZoneRenderer on a zone switch, so previouslyVisible (fog dimming) resets — revisiting a zone re-explores it. Persist per-zone visibility (e.g. keep a renderer/fog grid per zone, or move fog state into the zone/ECS) so explored areas stay remembered across transitions.
close_reason: Per-zone fog memory persists across zone transitions: hoisted the 'previously seen' Grid out of KotileZoneRenderer into a host-owned ZoneFog (one grid per zone, reused on return) and inject it into the renderer, so the rebuild on a zone change no longer wipes exploration. 3 ZoneFog tests (234 total). Save/load persistence of fog filed as krogue-k77.

title: Optional: simulate adjacent zones (chase across transitions)
description: Extension of ADR-0008's active-only model. Make the simulated-zone set a seam: a provider -> Set<zoneId> (default {currentZoneId}); zone-scoped systems iterate the set. A 'current + adjacent' policy lets monsters chase the player across a transition instead of freezing at the threshold. Also needs: zone-adjacency model, cross-zone HuntPlayer targeting, and boundary-crossing movement (update ZoneMember + Position together). Build the seam during 4e so this stays config-not-redesign.

title: Player death + HP feedback (no game-over yet)
description: Discovered during 4b-s5 testing: the player takes combat damage (Health drops by 20 on a zombie bump) but there is no HP display and no death/game-over handling -- the player is excluded from dead-removal, so reaching 0 HP does nothing. Pre-existing gap, outside the 4b ECS-migration steps. Needs: surface player HP, and decide behavior at 0 HP (game-over / restart). Likely after Phase 4b; relates to krogue-ui-layout for any HUD.
close_reason: Resolved by the UI toolkit: HP is surfaced via a live BarWidget (krogue-bhc) and 0 HP now triggers a modal game-over Dialog (Load last save / Quit) that freezes the world (krogue-wh9). CombatSystem still spares the player from despawn; death is handled at the UI/host layer rather than by removing the entity.
